items.rationale: Tiling labour to reinstate the ~3 m² panel (2.4×0.85 m wall plus 2.4×0.4 m plinth) within the damage area. Upper customary rate of about €70/m² gross.
One hole through a new tile for the pipe is necessary making good; priced at the prior level of about €65.
Replacement tiles matching the cheapest-range originals in the same size; quantity fits the damaged area. Standard grade at about €30/m².
The soft patch of about 1 m² around the bend was built back up before tiling, so this is necessary repair.
Second tile material charge in a non-standard giant format. It duplicates pos. 3 and does not match the original size; excluded under 3.5(a), 3.5(d) and 3.5(e).
Matches the wall/plinth corner (2.4 m) plus the panel end against the side wall (~1.25 m). At roughly €9/m.
Duplicates the silicone joints, the quantity is inconsistent with the 3.6 m needed, and it is premium grade. Excluded under 3.5(a), 3.5(d) and 3.5(e).
One travel charge per contractor per document is allowed under 7.4.2; prior level about €80.

Tiling and removal labour is largely already in the unit and flat-rate prices (7.4.1). Fourteen hours is excessive for a 3 m² panel; at most some hours for tile removal and the plinth would be accepted.
Cleaning the reinstated surface within the damage area is part of the repair cost (3.5(c)). It may, however, be treated as already included in the tiling rate.
The wet plasterboard boxing is in the damage area; its removal is demolition/opening-up cost.

items.description: Removal and disposal of damaged insulation
items.rationale: The wet mineral wool was removed and taken away by the tiler. This is a separate disposal from the container waste; prior level about €74.
The damp render behind the ~3 m² panel was hacked off; the quantity is consistent with the damage.
Attic gable staining dates from the roof re-felting years ago and is unrelated to the cellar leak (3.5(b)).
The cover ring cracked when the tiles came off, so replacing it is making good (5.2.6). A small standard part.
Undoing the leaking joint, fitting a new olive and reassembling. Earlier cases paid for joint repair as part of the escape-of-water claim.
Technical drying supported by moisture readings over about 8 days, so 7 days invoiced is consistent (5.2.7). Roughly €30/day.
Flat surcharge, payable only if attributable to materials actually used (olive, sealing paste) under 7.4.4. Small amount.
Replaces the metre of sodden lagging like-for-like; prior about €22/m.
Container for the tiles, render and board is debris removal (5.2.1); prior about €60.
